plan: [ In a second-price sealed-bid auction with independent private values, the weakly dominant strategy is to bid your true value. There is no prior history to adjust for, and values are redrawn each round. Underbidding risks losing profitable wins; overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth if others bid high. Therefore, to maximize expected profit, bid exactly my value of $10. ]

[ In a 3-bidder second-price sealed-bid auction, truth-telling is weakly dominant. Overbidding risks winning at a price above value; underbidding risks losing when winning would be profitable. With $0.1 increments, bid exactly your value: 30.0. This ensures you win whenever the highest competing bid is below 30 and pay that second-highest bid, guaranteeing nonnegative surplus and maximizing expected profit. No history to adapt this round; values are independently redrawn, so no strategic shading advantage. ]

[ In a second-price sealed-bid auction with independent private values, bidding your true value is weakly dominant. Overbidding risks winning when the second-highest bid exceeds your value (negative profit), while underbidding only reduces the chance of winning when it would be profitable. Payment, if you win, equals the second-highest bid, unaffected by truthful bidding. With no exploitable history (round 1 of 1) and uniform values, the optimal strategy is to bid exactly your value to maximize expected profit. ]
